headline: Sleep debt is today's story — protect it, and keep the run genuinely easy.
body_state: Readiness 61.5/100 (moderate), driven by sleep: 6.3h last night (score 66) on top of 26h of 14-day debt — that's the red flag, not training. Garmin composite reads lower (52, status "Recovery"). HRV 45ms is balanced, body battery 47 but recharged well overnight (+44), stress avg only 15. 7-day load 523, anaerobic-focus. Nothing here says stop training — it says protect sleep and don't add intensity on top of it.
session: Already banked this morning: "Un1t" class, 46min, avg HR 132, 69.7% of it in zone 3 — a real moderate-hard stimulus, still unrated in RPE. Still on the plan: 7km easy @ 4:51-5:20/km. Given the sleep debt and one session already in the bank, run this at the slow end of that band, cap HR near 130, and hold cadence 168-172 spm — yesterday's "easy" run sat at 157.6 spm and 89.7% zone 3, which is exactly the pattern to break today.
recent: The last 5 days repeat the same grey-zone pattern fitness.json flags as your #1 limiter: three "easy"-labeled sessions (Aug 7 long run, Aug 10 5km, this morning's Un1t) ran 69-90% zone-3 time each. Aug 7's progressive long run closed at 179bpm/threshold effort and readiness crashed to 23 the next check, training status flipped to "Unproductive." Cadence has stayed 157-163 spm across all of them, still under the 168-172 target set yesterday. The lever is the same every day: start slower than feels necessary.
focus: Protect sleep — go to bed ~60 min earlier for the next two weeks (26h debt built up).
Make today's easy run actually easy: slow end of 4:51-5:20/km, HR capped ~130, cadence 168-172.
Log RPE on this morning's Un1t — unrated sessions are invisible to load tracking.
